extractor.note: The reduction is here a presupposed starting point rather than a topic: the editors' introduction dates its arrival between the early time-texts and Bernau, and the manuscripts begin from it. The one place it is itself at work is the reduction to primal sensuality in Text Nr. 14.

coverage_note: Covers the sections in which the theme's terms occur - editors' introduction III and IV, Text Nr. 7 § 4, Text Nr. 12 § 1, Text Nr. 13 § 3, Text Nr. 14 § 1 and Text Nr. 15 § 1 - read in full, together with Text Nr. 1 § 1, Text Nr. 14 § 2 and editors' introduction V as context for the absences. Parts I to III and the supplements were not read in full.

units.claim: Following the introduction of the transcendental-phenomenological reduction, the relation between absolute consciousness and the sensation-datum was re-determined as a constitutive relation.
units.quote: Second, following the introduction of the transcendental-phenomenological reduction, the relation between "absolute" consciousness and sensation-datum was re-determined as a constitutive relation.

units.claim: The publication of Ideas I, with its systematic account of the phenomenological reduction, falls between the last early time-texts and the first Bernau manuscripts, and its findings entered them.
units.quote: Between the last early time-texts and the first Bernau manuscripts (1911–1917) falls the publication of *Ideas I*, with its systematic account of the phenomenological reduction, transcendental idealism, the noetic-noematic correlation, and the introduction of the pure ego. These new findings entered the Bernau time-manuscripts.

units.claim: Husserl often reflects on the phenomenological reduction and transcendental idealism in treating the constitutive function of time-consciousness.
units.quote: Husserl often reflects on the phenomenological reduction and transcendental idealism in treating the constitutive function of time-consciousness

units.claim: In the pure immanence after the phenomenological reduction no "we" and no plurality of subjects is first given, only the stream of experiences and the pure ego of this stream.
units.quote: In the pure immanence (after phenomenological reduction), no "we," no plurality of subjects is first given—only the stream of experiences and the pure ego of this stream.

units.claim: In transcendental reflection the ur-impressional data, the fading-modifications and the apprehension-functions are found.
units.quote: In transcendental reflection we find ur-impressional data, the fading-modifications, and also the apprehension-functions.

units.claim: In the deeper, second-level transcendental reflection the gaze turns to the transverse rows of givenness-modes and holds them through their modifications.
units.quote: In the deeper transcendental reflection (second level), the gaze turns to the transverse rows (the continua of givenness-modes) and holds them through their modifications.

units.claim: Husserl begins from the phenomenological reduction, considering the stream of experiences as a living, necessarily mobile present with its structure of ur-presence and horizon.
units.quote: Husserl begins from the phenomenological reduction, considering the stream of experiences: a "living," necessarily mobile "present" with its structure of ur-presence and "horizon" of just-having-been and a future.

units.claim: A further methodological reduction within the phenomenological reduction, the reduction to primal sensuality, abstracts from the ego and everything egoic.
units.quote: Husserl introduces a crucial methodological reduction within the phenomenological reduction: the reduction to "primal sensuality" (*ursprüngliche Sensualität*). This is an abstraction from the ego and everything egoic — though only an abstraction, an important one.

units.claim: Sensory drives are excluded as well because they bring the ego into play, leaving the completely egoless sensory tendencies of association and reproduction.
units.quote: Sensory drives are affections toward the ego, passive reactions — but we now also exclude these, since they bring the ego into play. We distinguish the "completely egoless" sensory tendencies: sensory tendencies of association and reproduction, and the horizon-formations they determine.

units.claim: The phenomenological reduction is the return to the stream of pure experiences and the pure ego, followed by a further return to the primal consciousness constituting immanent temporal objectivities.
units.quote: Through phenomenological reduction: the return to the stream of pure experiences and the pure ego, to immanent being whose necessary form is "phenomenological time" — and then the further return to the primal consciousness constituting immanent temporal objectivities.

absences.expected_because: This is the opening analysis of the published manuscripts, where the field of ur-presentation and attentional turning is entered, and it names nothing that would have secured that field.

The section immediately follows the reduction to primal sensuality, which was expressly an abstraction from the ego, and restores the ego as non-temporal functioning pole without naming the reduction it reverses.
